question: What is the main object of the Superannuation Industry (Supervision) Act 1993?
relevant_excerpts: The main object of this Act is to make provision for the prudent management of certain superannuation funds, approved deposit funds and pooled superannuation trusts and for their supervision by APRA, ASIC and the Commissioner of Taxation.

question: What is the maximum number of members permitted for a self managed superannuation fund under the basic conditions?
relevant_excerpts: it has fewer than 5 members;

question: Under what condition may one member of a self managed superannuation fund be an employee of another member?
relevant_excerpts: unless the members concerned are relatives;

question: What requirements must a superannuation fund satisfy to become a regulated superannuation fund?
relevant_excerpts: A regulated superannuation fund is a superannuation fund in respect of which subsections (2) to (4) have been complied with.
The superannuation fund must have a trustee.

Either of the following must apply: (a) the trustee of the fund must be a constitutional corporation pursuant to a requirement contained in the governing rules; (b) the governing rules must provide that the sole or primary purpose of the fund is the provision of old-age pensions.
The trustee or trustees must have given to APRA, or such other body or person as is specified in the regulations, a written notice
signed by the trustee or each trustee; electing that this Act is to apply in relation to the fund.

question: What investment factors must an SMSF trustee consider when formulating and reviewing the fund's investment strategy?
relevant_excerpts: the risk involved in making, holding and realising, and the likely return from, the fund’s investments
regard to its objectives and its expected cash flow requirements;
the composition of the fund’s investments as a whole including the extent to which the investments are diverse or involve the fund in being exposed to risks from inadequate diversification;
the liquidity of the fund’s investments, having regard to its expected cash flow requirements;
the ability of the fund to discharge its existing and prospective liabilities;

question: What retirement-related purpose is included as a core purpose under the sole purpose test?
relevant_excerpts: the provision of benefits for each member of the fund on or after the member’s retirement from any business, trade, profession, vocation, calling, occupation or employment in which the member was engaged

question: To whom is a regulated superannuation fund prohibited from lending money or providing financial assistance?
relevant_excerpts: lend money of the fund to: (i) a member of the fund; or (ii) a relative of a member of the fund;
give any other financial assistance using the resources of the fund to: (i) a member of the fund; or (ii) a relative of a member of the fund.

question: Which assets may a fund with fewer than five members acquire from a related party under the exceptions in section 66(2)?
relevant_excerpts: Subsection (1) does not prohibit a trustee or investment manager acquiring an asset from a related party of the fund if: (a) the asset is a listed security acquired at market value; or (b) if the fund is a superannuation fund with fewer than 5 members—the asset is business real property of the related party acquired at market value;

question: What time and fund-value limits apply when a trustee temporarily borrows money to make a required payment to a beneficiary?
relevant_excerpts: the period of the borrowing does not exceed 90 days;
if the borrowing were to take place, the total amount borrowed by the trustee would not exceed 10% of the value of the assets of the fund.

question: What records relating to trustee decisions and trustee changes must be retained for at least 10 years?
relevant_excerpts: If a superannuation entity has a group of individual trustees, the trustees must keep, and retain for at least 10 years, minutes of all meetings of the trustees at which matters affecting the entity were considered.
if the trustee is an individual—the trustee must keep, and retain for at least 10 years, a record of all decisions made by the trustee in respect of matters affecting the entity.

Each trustee of a superannuation entity must ensure that up-to-date records of: (a) all changes of trustees of the entity; and (b) all changes of directors of any corporate trustee of the entity; and (c) all consents given under section 118; are kept and retained for at least 10 years.
